title: Composition coherence for adjoint restriction-kernel diagrams
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be small sites with abelian sheaf categories [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $v:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ be functors whose precomposition preserves abelian sheaves. Write $R(G)(W)=G(uW)$ and $R_v(H)(W)=H(vW)$ for these precomposition functors. Suppose $L\dashv R$ and $M\dashv R_v$ are additive adjunctions with exact left adjoints. Let $m:V\to T$, $m':V'\to T'$, and $m'':V''\to T''$ be monomorphisms in the three sites. Let $t:T'\to uT$, $s:V'\to uV$, $t':T''\to vT'$, and $s':V''\to vV'$ satisfy $u(m)s=tm'$ and $v(m')s'=t'm''$. For cochain complexes $I,J,P$ on $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ respectively, let $h:LI\to J$ and $k:MJ\to P$ be chain maps. Define the restriction-kernel diagram $D_m(I)=[\ker(I(T)\to I(V))\to I(T)\to I(V)]$ and its adjoint diagram maps as in [lem-pur-support-pair-chain-coherence](1). Then the diagram map for $k\circ M(h)$ and the composite data $(v\circ u,v(t)\circ t',v(s)\circ s')$ equals the composite of the diagram maps for $h$ and $k$, under the unit-compatible identification of the composite adjunction with $(M\circ L)\dashv(R\circ R_v)$. The same identity holds on cohomology for derived coefficient morphisms represented on bounded-below injective complexes, independently of representative choices as in [lem-pur-support-pair-chain-coherence](2).

proof.text: For a sheaf morphism h:LF→G and k:MG→H, Adjunction.comp_homEquiv and naturality of the two Hom bijections identify the transpose of M(h)≫k with the transpose of h followed by R applied to the transpose of k. Evaluate at T, and use naturality of the transpose of k along t:T′→uT: G(t)≫c(T′)=c(uT)≫H(v(t)). Contravariant functoriality H(t′≫v(t))=H(v(t))≫H(t′) then proves the composition formula for the ambient sections. Repeat with V,s,s′ for restricted sections. These formulas imply that φ≫ψ satisfies the composite support-pair map condition. Any χ satisfying that condition has the same second and third components. Its first component equals that of φ≫ψ by their commutation with the kernel inclusion, which is monic. This proves chain-level equality directly from the definitions.

source.place: Section 9, Theorem 9.4, pp. 65-67, functoriality in the pair; Stacks sites.tex Tag 03CB for composition of site morphisms and adjunction transposition

proof.text: The composite pair square follows by functoriality: (s′≫v(s))≫v(u(m)) = s′≫v(s≫u(m)) = s′≫v(m′≫t) = (s′≫v(m′))≫v(t) = m″≫(t′≫v(t)). Composite continuity is Functor.isContinuous_comp; composite finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation are comp_preservesFiniteLimits and comp_preservesFiniteColimits. Hence the representative-independence clause of [lem-pur-support-pair-chain-coherence] applies to the composite adjunction and to I,N.

source.place: Section 9, Theorem 9.4, pp. 65-67, functoriality and independence of injective representatives; Stacks derived.tex Tag 070I

proof.text: Put q=M(h)≫k. Functoriality of standardDerivedQ, the hypothesis Q(k)=b, and the displayed hypothesis on Q(g) show Q(q)=Q(g). By Step 1, φ≫ψ satisfies the composite support-pair condition for q, whereas χ satisfies it for g by hypothesis. Apply the equal-derived-representatives clause of [lem-pur-support-pair-chain-coherence] to q,g and these two diagrams. It directly gives supportCohomologyEqual (φ≫ψ) χ; the hypotheses needed are exactly bounded-below injectivity of I and N. No new representative or homotopy construction is needed.
